part_b_findings.topic: Plugin Root by Manifest-Anchored Ascent; Env Var Advisory Only
part_b_findings.priority_reason: Coordinator: load-bearing claim -- if ascent needs no undocumented behaviour, it removes ADR-009a branch 2's dependency on unverified FR-14a item 2. Check hard.
part_b_findings.load_bearing_claim: 'branch 2 is implementable whichever way the spike returns, because the primary mechanism never consults the environment' (OAQ3, line ~1115)
part_b_findings.verification_method: (1) Confirmed PluginRootResolver does not exist anywhere in the live repo (repo-wide search, zero matches outside docs) -- correctly framed by the HLD as a proposed ADR-012 design, not existing code, and SS13a independently makes the same disclosure for plugin_api/. (2) Logical soundness check: __file__-based upward directory ascent is standard Python behaviour (Path(__file__).resolve().parent, walked until a sentinel file is found) that does not depend on Claude Code propagating CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT into the spawned process's os.environ at all -- it needs nothing from the host beyond __file__ being set, which CPython guarantees for any imported module. The claim is therefore not resting on unverified host behaviour.
part_b_findings.caveat_check: The disclosed limitation ('__file__ anchoring does not survive zipimport or a frozen bundle') is honestly stated and correctly scoped as inapplicable, since ADR-008 ships a git repo tree, not a zipimport/frozen bundle.
part_b_findings.result: The load-bearing claim holds. It is a sound engineering argument, not an overclaim -- it correctly identifies that filesystem ascent and environment-variable reading are independent mechanisms, so removing the primary dependency on the latter genuinely de-risks ADR-009a branch 2 regardless of the FR-14a item 2 spike result.

part_b_findings.topic: Coverage-Complete Discovery Replaces the Silent Cap
part_b_findings.priority_reason: Coordinator: must make silent package-dropping inexpressible, not merely discouraged.
part_b_findings.claim_checked: 'the allocator returns the pair (selected, dropped) and build_call_graph requires the manifest as a non-optional constructor argument. There is therefore no code path that removes a file from the candidate set without that removal appearing in the manifest, because the graph cannot be constructed from selected alone.'
part_b_findings.verification_method: Design-logic check (this is a proposed v2.0.0 design, not yet-implemented code -- correctly framed as 'Chosen' rather than as an existing-code fact, consistent with the rest of the ADR set). A non-optional constructor parameter is a real structural guarantee in a typed/enforced construction path: if DiscoveryManifest is mandatory to build the graph object, no caller can obtain a graph without also obtaining the manifest, which by RECONCILE's invariant (analysed_n + dropped_n == discovered_n) makes total silent dropping structurally unreachable, not merely policy-discouraged.
part_b_findings.cross_check: All 4 listed truncator line-citations (config.py:11; call_graph_builder_legacy.py:64/:76; code_graph_analyzer.py:73/:137/:154/:169; code-graph-analyzer.py:68/:120/:137/:152) re-verified byte-exact this pass, identical to pass 1's findings.
part_b_findings.result: The 'structurally impossible' framing is an accurate description of what a non-optional-constructor-argument design achieves (in contrast to a convention or a lint rule, which would only be 'discouraged'). No overclaim found.

part_b_findings.priority_reason: Coordinator: must not reintroduce any fixed per-call wall-clock timeout, which NFR-2 forbids.
part_b_findings.verification_method: Direct source read of all 7 cited lines across 5 files
part_b_findings.polarity_check: The Chosen mechanisms (attempt-count abort, lease renewal, convergence-hash signal, circuit breaker, slow-call-rate trip) explicitly replace the task-aborting timeouts at the cited sites -- they do not add a new fixed-timeout mechanism. The ADR draws an explicit, correctly-reasoned line: per-socket-read timeouts remain permitted (bounded to one I/O call, feed a circuit breaker, never abort the enclosing pipeline task) versus banned task-aborting deadlines -- and this distinction matches NFR-2's own quoted AC ('any timeout present must be configurable and default to unbounded or user-overridable').
part_b_findings.result: No fixed per-call wall-clock timeout is reintroduced by the Chosen design. The one exception (socket-level) is correctly scoped and is not the kind of timeout NFR-2 forbids.

fifth_truncator_reasoning_check.instruction: Check the 'sharper instance' argument -- a return False indistinguishable from a genuine 'no code files exist' -- for whether it holds.
fifth_truncator_reasoning_check.claim: Site 5 (build_dependency_resolver/parsers.py:682/696) is a 'different purpose, same defect class -- and a sharper instance' than sites 1-4, because a truncated boolean carries zero residual information while a truncated list/graph is at least externally inspectable.
fifth_truncator_reasoning_check.verified_against: Direct source read of parsers.py:675-704 (both this pass and pass 1, identical): max_files_scanned=1000 at :682; 'if files_scanned > max_files_scanned: return False' at :696, inside a bounded BFS whose only other return path is the natural queue-exhaustion False.
fifth_truncator_reasoning_check.reasoning_check: Holds. Sites 1-4 return a list of discovered files; even without instrumentation, that list's length can be compared against an independently-obtainable total file count (as the HLD itself demonstrates by independently re-counting 411 Python files) to detect truncation after the fact. Site 5 returns a single bit with no accompanying count, so the two False cases (genuine absence vs a give-up-early cap) are provably indistinguishable to any caller, with no external cross-check available even in principle without re-instrumenting the function. The comparison to ADR-015's PARSE_ERROR-vs-no-match conflation is apt and consistently applied.
fifth_truncator_reasoning_check.disposition_check: The HLD does NOT fold site 5 into FR-9a's scope (correctly reasoned: different consumer, different purpose, would expand a critical-path item for no FR-10 benefit) and instead records it as a named v2.1 follow-on under ADR-013's general principle. This is a defensible, non-overreaching scope boundary, not a hallucination or a quiet omission.
